text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- President Hosni Mubarak received a comprehensive report on the results of Egyptian contacts with France and the United States on developments in the peace process and the inauspicious circumstances it is going through. Foreign Minister Amr Moussa said he submitted to Mubarak a report on his visit to Paris and his talks with President Jacques Chirac and his telephone conversation on Wednesday with U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher on peace and Israeli settlements.

- Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri said prices of goods and services will not rise and that the government will impose no new taxes in the coming year. He said this would be in the statement the government makes on Monday to parliament.
- President Mubarak met the Slovak foreign minister, who said they discussed bilateral relations and the peace process in the Middle East.
- Flights were held up for three hours at Cairo airport on Thursday morning because of thick fog.

- Industry Minister Suleiman Reda witnessed on Wednesday a prpearatory meeting on setting up a giant project to produce fertilisers. The project will cost about 3.6 billion pounds ($1.1 billion), to be financed by Egyptians and Arabs.
- Signs of a crisis in Israeli-American relations.
- President Mubarak will have talks tomorrow with Greek President Costis Stephanopoulos, who will arrive in Alexandria today for a three-day visit to Egypt.

- An appeals court in Giza upheld the decision of a lower court to suspend the separation of academic Nasr Abu Zaid and his wife. (In a parallel case the courts have upheld the decision to separate Abu Zaid from his wife on the grounds that his writings make him an apostate).

- The mobile phone service will be expanded in 1997. Twenty-six more base stations will be in operation in Cairo by the end of January and from January the service will start in Alexandria, the north coast, Luxor and Aswan.
- Egypt and Slovakia will sign investment protection and double taxation agreements.
- Forty residents of social welfare homes, 13 elderly people and 27 children, had food poisoning after eating meat donated to their homes. Five of them are in intensive care.
